title: A Three-Week IB Maths AI Revision Plan for November
summary: IB Maths AI revision plan for November: prioritise weak topics, practise with timed papers, and protect rest across three weeks while balancing IB subjects.
body_markdown:
This **IB Maths AI revision plan** follows a simple sequence: diagnose gaps in week one, strengthen them in week two, then rehearse the examination in week three. It suits SL and HL students preparing for November while balancing other IB subjects.


Three weeks can feel uncomfortably short. Selective revision makes that time useful: identify where marks disappear, practise the relevant skills and check whether improvements survive under pressure.


### Your three-week overview


Week Main priority Mathematics workload


Week one Diagnose and prioritise 45-75 minutes on five days


Week two Repair weaknesses and mix topics 60-90 minutes on five days


Week three Timed rehearsal and recovery Two or three timed papers plus reviews


Check the[November IB Maths examination dates](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/ib-math-exam-dates-november-2026) for your session against your other examinations. Choose realistic mathematics slots before filling your calendar.


Prepare these essentials:


- Your approved graphical display calculator and correct formula booklet
- A topic list and mistake log
- Access to the[Maths AI Questionbank](https://www.revisiondojo.com/features/questionbank)
- Protected periods for timed practice
- One lighter evening each week


### Week one: diagnose before you revise


Starting with the first syllabus topic feels orderly, but it gives every topic equal attention. Your diagnostic should decide where time goes.


Complete a mixed set covering number and algebra, functions, geometry and trigonometry, statistics and probability, and calculus. Include HL content if applicable. Work for 45-60 minutes without notes, using your calculator and formula booklet.


Mark each question and classify lost marks:


- **Knowledge:** you did not understand the concept.
- **Process:** you could not choose a method.
- **Calculator:** you could not execute the calculation efficiently.
- **Communication:** working, notation or interpretation was incomplete.
- **Timing:** your method took too long.


These categories suggest different remedies. Calculating a probability incorrectly requires different practice from calculating it correctly but failing to interpret it.


### Choose three priority topics


Label topics red, amber or green. Red means unreliable performance, amber means partial understanding, and green means generally accurate work. Limit your red list to three topics so the priorities remain actionable.


Use[syllabus-organised Study Notes](https://www.revisiondojo.com/features/notes) to repair specific concepts. For an unclear step, ask the[Jojo AI Tutor for guided help](https://www.revisiondojo.com/features/jojo-ai-tutor) , then attempt another question independently.


Finish the week with a short mixed set. Keep persistent weaknesses on the red list and move improving topics into regular mixed practice.


### Week two: turn weaknesses into usable marks


A practical 75-minute session has four parts:


- 10 minutes reviewing formulas or yesterday's errors
- 35 minutes answering focused questions
- 20 minutes completing mixed questions
- 10 minutes marking and updating your log


Focused practice develops the method. Mixed practice checks whether you recognise when to use it. Alternate red and amber topics rather than spending the entire week on one chapter.


Use[Flashcards with spaced repetition](https://www.revisiondojo.com/features/flashcards) for definitions, notation and conditions. Keep written problem-solving central: remembering a formula and applying it are separate skills.


### Rehearse calculator decisions


Practise choosing a model, entering information accurately, recording working and interpreting the output. Obtaining a regression equation, for example, may be followed by explaining a parameter or assessing whether an estimate is appropriate.


Check the[calculator models and skills needed for IB mathematics](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/ib-math-exam-calculator-allowed-models-skills) , then rehearse commands on your examination device.


A student revises beside a calculator while another person tucks a second calculator into bed for a break.


*One calculator receives an unusually comfortable study break.*


Near the week's end, complete a timed half-paper or custom mixed test using[Test Builder and Exam Mode](https://www.revisiondojo.com/features/test-builder) . Separate conceptual mistakes from pressure-related errors when marking. The next session should address the cause you actually found.


### Week three: rehearse the examination


Shift towards complete attempts, pacing and clear solutions. SL students sit two papers; HL students also sit Paper 3.


The established durations are 1 hour 30 minutes for each SL paper, 2 hours for HL Papers 1 and 2, and 1 hour 15 minutes for HL Paper 3. Confirm arrangements for your session using your school's information and the[IB Maths paper lengths guide](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/ib-math-paper-length-aa-ai-times) .


Schedule two complete timed attempts. HL students can add Paper 3 if their wider timetable allows. Use[Predicted Papers](https://www.revisiondojo.com/features/predicted-papers) or a balanced paper in Exam Mode as practice, without treating predicted content as guaranteed examination coverage.


After each attempt, take a break, mark carefully and identify why marks were lost. Redo incorrect questions without the solution, then answer two related questions for any conceptual weakness. A score describes the attempt; error analysis directs tomorrow's work.


### Keep the final 48 hours manageable


Review your mistake log, calculator routines and recurring question types. The[Maths AI exam study plan](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/how-to-study-effectively-for-ib-math-applications-and-interpretation-ai-exams) offers a broader technique check.


Reduce heavy practice, protect sleep and confirm your examination time, location and permitted equipment. Familiar routines help remove avoidable uncertainty.


### Balance mathematics with other subjects


When another examination approaches, shorten a mathematics session to 30 minutes: answer three targeted questions, mark them and update your log. Resume longer practice when your timetable permits.


Keep one lighter evening each week. Schedule complete papers when you can concentrate, with time afterwards for review. An unfinished marking session leaves the most useful feedback unused.


### Make the remaining days useful


Begin with one diagnostic set and let its results guide your next session. RevisionDojo brings the process together: Questionbank for repair, Study Notes and AI Chat for explanations, Flashcards for recall, grading tools for feedback, and Predicted Papers or Mock Exams for rehearsal. Tutors can support persistent gaps, while the Coursework Library supports wider IB work.


Each day needs a clear purpose: understand a weakness, practise a decision or rehearse performance.
